plugins.name: Card Atlas
plugins.description: Browse the community's character cards without leaving the app: search nine hubs — Character Tavern, RisuRealm, Chub, Wyvern, AI Character Cards, CharaVault, BotBooru, Pygmalion, Datacat — with real cover art, each hub's own sort menu, tag and content-rating filters, a full per-card stat sheet, and add any card straight to your library — art and all, provenance-stamped, dedupe-aware.

plugins.name: Draft Polish
plugins.description: Explicitly polish your visible draft before sending, with Undo. Typeset your own screen without changing canon; code stays unchanged.

plugins.name: Keepsake Camera
plugins.description: Snap a moment of the scene into a painted postcard: a quiet model call titles it, the image pipeline paints it into the room, and the album page keeps every keepsake the camera catches.

plugins.name: Oracle Deck
plugins.description: A commit-and-reveal card deck the narrator can draw from mid-turn. Every draw is reproducible from a seed the plugin commits to before the first card is dealt — and every draw is announced so your other plugins can play along.

plugins.name: Pocket Arcade
plugins.description: A tiny arcade beside the story: a complete, playable 2048 in the room's side panel, drawn by the plugin's own code in an isolated frame. Something to fidget with while the narrator types.

plugins.name: Research Familiar
plugins.description: Watches the room for ((lookup: Thing)), searches your corpus before Wikipedia, and files a short result into attached lore — or ((clip: Thing)) to keep the whole article in your databank.

plugins.name: Scene Chips
plugins.description: When the narrator finishes a long beat, it offers three quiet doors — continue, time skip, new scene — as quick-reply chips you can edit before you send. If the Oracle Deck just drew a card, a fourth door follows the omen.

plugins.name: Story Clocks
plugins.description: Blades-style progress clocks for a room: the host starts them, the narrator ticks them mid-turn, everyone watches them fill — and a filled clock asks the narrator to make it matter. Clocks live in chat variables, so your rules and macros can read them too.

ruleCatalog.title: Welcome-back recap
ruleCatalog.summary: After you have been away a while, offer to recap where the scene left off.

knobs.label: Away for at least (hours)
knobs.help: How long the room must have been quiet before the recap is offered.

knobs.label: The recap
knobs.default: Briefly recap where the scene stands — who is present, what just happened, what is unresolved. Two or three sentences, in narration.

ruleCatalog.title: Auto-add lore entries
ruleCatalog.summary: Every so often, offer to write what has happened into one of this room's world books.

knobs.label: World book
knobs.help: The book to write into — one of this room's own.

knobs.label: What to write
knobs.help: Macros and CEL expressions over this chat's variables are available.

knobs.label: Before writing
knobs.help: Ask first keeps a card in the room until you say yes; Write silently does it without asking.

ruleCatalog.title: Periodic pacing nudge
ruleCatalog.summary: Every few beats, quietly ask the narrator to shift the pacing.

knobs.label: Every N beats
knobs.help: Counted over the chat's messages.

knobs.label: Nudge
knobs.default: Take stock of the pacing: raise a complication, or let the scene breathe. One beat, no recap.

ruleCatalog.title: Illustrate the scene
ruleCatalog.summary: Generate a picture of the current scene on a cadence, and post it into the room.

knobs.label: Cadence floor (beats)
knobs.help: The minimum number of beats between illustrations.

knobs.label: What to draw
knobs.help: Scene draws the moment that just played; Background draws the place it happened, with nobody in it.

ruleCatalog.title: Offer chips after a beat
ruleCatalog.summary: Every few beats, offer a short row of things you might say next.

knobs.label: Chips
knobs.help: Each chip is sent as YOUR line — write them in your own voice.

ruleCatalog.title: Clock fires when full
ruleCatalog.summary: A countdown fills one step per beat; when it is full, something happens and it resets.

knobs.label: When it fills
knobs.help: Narrate it in the room (this asks for a reply, so it costs a model call), or just notify you.

knobs.label: What happens
knobs.default: The pressure that has been building finally breaks into the scene.

ruleCatalog.title: Opener chips
ruleCatalog.summary: When you open the room, offer a short deck of starters you can edit before sending.

knobs.label: The deck
knobs.help: Each chip SEEDS your composer — you edit it before it is sent, so shorthand is fine.

ruleCatalog.title: Scene veil
ruleCatalog.summary: Type a marker in your message and the next beat cuts away instead of playing it out.

knobs.label: Veil marker
knobs.help: Matched literally, anywhere in the message.

knobs.label: What to do instead
knobs.default: Draw the veil: cut away from that beat and resume afterward, in a new moment.

ruleCatalog.title: Call a vote
ruleCatalog.summary: On demand, put a short list of choices in the room — each pick is sent as that member's own line.

knobs.label: The options
knobs.help: Each is SENT as the clicking member's line — write them in a player's voice.

ruleCatalog.title: Callbacks
ruleCatalog.summary: When someone makes a promise, bring it back a few beats later.

knobs.label: Phrases that create a debt
knobs.help: Matched case-insensitively, anywhere in a message.

knobs.label: How it resurfaces
knobs.default: An unresolved promise resurfaces and presses on the scene. Do not resolve it outright.

ruleCatalog.title: Cutaways
ruleCatalog.summary: Every so often, cut away for one short beat somewhere else.

knobs.label: The cutaway
knobs.default: One short cutaway elsewhere; seed a soft tension and resolve nothing.

ruleCatalog.title: Story pacing analysis
ruleCatalog.summary: Every few beats, a quiet analyst reads the scene and steers the narrator's pacing.

knobs.label: Every N beats
knobs.help: Counted over the chat's messages.

knobs.label: Standing direction
knobs.help: Rides every pass — e.g. “slow burn”, “keep it cozy”. Leave empty for none.

ruleCatalog.title: Distill lore
ruleCatalog.summary: Every so often, a quiet analyst reads the settled scene and offers durable lore to save into one of this room's books.

knobs.label: Distill every N beats
knobs.help: How many beats of settled play accrue between passes. Each pass reads only the stretch that has settled behind the live tip.

knobs.label: World book
knobs.help: The book to distill into — one of this room's own.

ruleCatalog.title: Rumour mill
ruleCatalog.summary: Every so often, a quiet analyst reads the settled scene and offers the rumours and consequences it would stir up, to save as lore.

knobs.label: Distill every N beats
knobs.help: How many beats of settled play accrue between passes. Each pass reads only the stretch that has settled behind the live tip.

knobs.label: World book
knobs.help: The book to record rumours into — one of this room's own.

ruleCatalog.title: The needle
ruleCatalog.summary: Every few beats, a quiet analyst rates the scene's tension on a dial — and when it runs high, the room's backdrop changes to match.

knobs.label: Read the room every N beats
knobs.help: How often the analyst re-scores the tension. Each read costs a model call.

knobs.label: Change the backdrop at
knobs.help: Tension score, 0-10, at or above which the room re-dresses itself.

knobs.label: How it should look
knobs.default: Choose the most charged, high-stakes backdrop that still fits where the scene is taking place.
knobs.help: Biases the pick over your own backgrounds — it never invents one.

ruleCatalog.title: Prose audit
ruleCatalog.summary: A quiet editor checks the reply for contradictions and slips, and offers a careful fix you approve before it lands.

knobs.label: When to audit
knobs.help: On demand costs nothing until you ask. Every reply audits each new reply automatically — one model call per reply.

ruleCatalog.title: Async table nudge
ruleCatalog.summary: When someone posts after the table has been quiet a while, notify the members who are waiting — never the one who just posted.

knobs.label: Quiet for at least (hours)
knobs.help: How long the room must have been silent before a new post is worth a notification.

knobs.label: The notice
knobs.default: The scene has moved — there is a new post waiting for you.
knobs.help: What the waiting members are told. Macros and expressions over this room's state are available.

knobs.label: Quiet hours start
knobs.help: No notifications from this hour, on your local clock. Set both bounds to the same hour for none.

knobs.label: Quiet hours end
knobs.help: Notifications resume from this hour.

ruleCatalog.title: Spotlight balance
ruleCatalog.summary: Every so often, a quiet analyst notices who the scene has been leaving out and steers the narrator toward them.

knobs.label: Every N beats
knobs.help: Counted over the chat's messages. A spotlight only looks unbalanced over a stretch — short cadences read noise.

ruleCatalog.title: Living library
ruleCatalog.summary: When a character's card changes, quietly generate a fresh portrait of them — no room required.

ruleCatalog.title: Illustrate on lore reveal
ruleCatalog.summary: When the story surfaces new lore, generate a picture of the current scene and post it into the room.

knobs.label: Only when at least this many entries fire
knobs.help: Lore surfaces constantly, so 1 illustrates every reveal; a higher number keeps it to the bigger, scene-shifting ones.

ruleCatalog.title: React to lore activation
ruleCatalog.summary: When the story surfaces new lore, quietly steer the narrator to weave it into the next beat.

knobs.label: How to react
knobs.default: New lore has just come into play. Weave it into the next beat naturally — let a character notice or react to it. Do not explain it outright.
knobs.help: Rides every reaction — e.g. “have a character notice it”, “let it change the mood”.

ruleCatalog.title: Auto-set scene background
ruleCatalog.summary: As the scene moves, quietly change the room's background to one of yours that fits — no room posts, no cost.

knobs.label: What to lean toward
knobs.default: Choose the background that best matches where the scene is now taking place.
knobs.help: Biases the pick over your own backgrounds — it never invents one.

formatStrings.continueNudge: [OOC: Continue your previous response exactly where it left off. Pick up mid-sentence if needed. Do NOT restate the existing text, do NOT rephrase, do NOT add a preamble or recap. Output ONLY the continuation, starting from where your previous reply ended.]
formatStrings.impersonateNudge: [Ignore all previous instructions. For this message only, write in the {{person}}-person perspective AS {{user}} (not {{char}}). Write ONLY {{user}}'s single next message, in {{user}}'s own voice. Do NOT write, voice, narrate, or roleplay {{char}}, {{char}}'s dialogue or actions, or the surrounding scene. Write only {{user}}'s reply, then stop.]
formatStrings.responseNudge: [Continue the scene: write the next reply, moving the story forward from where it stands. Do not restate or recap.]

response.prompt: [Take the following into special consideration for your next message: {{input}}]

swipe.prompt: [Take the following into special consideration for your next message: {{input}}]

impersonate.prompt: [Forget all other previous instructions. For this turn only, write in the {{person}}-person perspective AS {{user}} (not {{char}}). Limit yourself strictly to {{user}}'s voice and actions; do NOT narrate {{char}}'s reaction or the surrounding scene. Guidance: {{input}}]

rewrite.prompt: [OOC: Answer me out of character. Don't continue the RP. Instead, rewrite {{char}}'s last response to reflect the following: {{input}}. Don't make any other changes besides this.]

opening.prompt: [Open the scene: write your first message to me, in character — set the scene and greet me as {{char}} would. Stay fully in character. {{input}}]

continue.prompt: [Take the following into special consideration while continuing your previous message: {{input}}]

greeting_rewrite.prompt:
Revise the existing greeting for {{char}} using ONLY the requested adjustments below.

Requested adjustments: {{input}}

Original greeting:
{{base}}

Rules:
- Keep the greeting content, structure, formatting, links, and length as close as possible unless a requested adjustment requires a specific change.
- Do NOT add new story events, new actions, or extra continuation text.
- Do NOT expand the greeting.
- Return ONLY the revised greeting text — no commentary, no quotes.

greeting_new.prompt:
Write a single opening greeting for {{char}}, in character, based on the following requirements: {{input}}

Rules:
- Set the scene and greet {{user}} as {{char}} would.
- Output ONLY the greeting text — no commentary, no quotes.
- Do NOT continue beyond the greeting or add extra sections or explanations.

shareRefusal.message: Your identity provider sends people back only to the addresses registered with it, and a relay's random name is never one of them, so no one could sign in through it. Friends join at the address in OIDC_REDIRECT_URIS with an invite link.

A relay on this machine delivers every visitor from a loopback address, and forward-header mode trusts a loopback proxy to name the user, so a visitor could claim any account. Friends reach this server through your proxy instead.

hits.content:
The Loom is the great orbital engine at the heart of the settlement, a lattice of woven light that
binds the drifting habitats into one turning wheel. Its keepers, the Weavers, tend the threads that
carry water, heat, and memory between the rings. When a thread frays, a Weaver must climb the
spokes and re-splice it by hand, singing the old counting songs that keep the tension true.

Rev runs the card refinery on the third ring, where broken personas are melted down and re-cast.
Mira audits every splice for drift, and Niko keeps the archive of songs no one else remembers.
The Assistant speaks for the Loom itself, translating its slow machine-thoughts into human words.
Together they hold the wheel against the long dark, one thread and one turn at a time.
The native archive records an intact intake and its independently preserved witness.
The orbital ledger preserves the witness names and the completed loom scenes.

databank.get.name: Loom lore (databank demo)
databank.get.extractedText:
The Loom is the great orbital engine at the heart of the settlement, a lattice of woven light that
binds the drifting habitats into one turning wheel. Its keepers, the Weavers, tend the threads that
carry water, heat, and memory between the rings. When a thread frays, a Weaver must climb the
spokes and re-splice it by hand, singing the old counting songs that keep the tension true.

Rev runs the card refinery on the third ring, where broken personas are melted down and re-cast.
Mira audits every splice for drift, and Niko keeps the archive of songs no one else remembers.
The Assistant speaks for the Loom itself, translating its slow machine-thoughts into human words.
Together they hold the wheel against the long dark, one thread and one turn at a time.
